question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\textrm E[X] = \dfrac {10}{3},$ compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14133689/assets/50e7428db936f89942d4c775d2dfe7691b853a9ca729e30c1958cb25b6c1e8d2.svg)
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2
$$

 

We compute $\textrm E[X^2],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{3}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot (8-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(8{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{8{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2})|}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{67}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{67}{6}-{(\frac{10}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
